Subject: Intermittent backpressure on batched generation endpoints — status page entry & customer comms

Hi Emma / ClearHarbor ops team —

Quick heads-up: we observed intermittent request backpressure affecting batched generation endpoints in us-west-1 starting ~09:05 PT. Symptoms: elevated p95 (requests taking 2–3x normal) for batched endpoints, transient 429s for heavy-concurrency clients, and a short window of queued requests that increased tail latency.

Impact: your batched inference pipelines that rely on >8 simultaneous streams may see slowed throughput for ~5–10 minutes while we engage mitigations. We do not believe data was lost or responses truncated — just delayed.

Immediate actions in flight: Sean is corralling an ops runbook to enable emergency burst pool and to adjust the autoscaler thresholds to reduce delay in pool expansion. We are also collecting KV cache and scheduler traces (attached) for root-cause.

We will post a brief status page notice now and follow up with a customer-facing blurb for you to reuse. ETA for next update: 30 minutes.

Attachments: incident-traces-20260915.zip (log bundle, 4MB)

Apologies for the disruption — we know throughput is critical for your pipelines.

— Hannah

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intermittent backpressure on batched generation endpoints — status page entry & customer comms

Emma — quick technical update (TL;DR: batched-only, mitigation applied):

What we found so far:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of short-lived autoscaler delay and a KV cache eviction storm when several large-batch workloads converged on the same pool. The eviction increased cold-start penalty for KV lookups and blocked some scheduler slots briefly.
- Single-stream endpoints and small-batch (<8) customers show normal behaviour; the issue is concentrated on batched endpoints using the legacy batch allocator.

Actions taken (09:25–09:34 PT):
1) Enabled emergency burst pool (pre-warmed instances) for affected hostpool in us-west-1 — traffic was gradually drained to it.
2) Temporarily relaxed batch coalescing for affected customers to reduce co-scheduling pressure.
3) Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for that hostpool to shrink the expansion delay.

Observed effect: p95 returning toward normal within ~6 minutes after burst pool activation; residual queued requests are being drained. No customer requests were dropped, only delayed.

Next steps:
- We will push a scheduler patch this week to harden against concurrent eviction storms.
- Postmortem with timeline and remediation plan will be shared within 72 hours.

I attached a small trace excerpt to the internal bundle for context.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal SRE
